name: Geneva Hollins
languages: French (song French, which she pronounces better than she understands)
equipment: .32 pocket pistol (Colt 1903, blued), 8 rounds loaded, in her handbag under the sheet music
Straight razor, pearl-handled, in her garter, which her mother gave her the day she started singing in clubs
Evening clothes: two gowns, one green and one black, and a pair of long gloves mended at the fingertips
A church hat with one small brave feather
Sheet music with the Gold Leaf's stamp, the band's book for her twelve numbers
A letter from a Chicago record company offering the Jules Ransom Orchestra, with Miss Geneva Hollins, vocal, a recording date on 12 November 1936
Card file of contacts: every club owner, bandleader, numbers banker, pastor and precinct captain on Eighteenth Street, in her own hand
features: Knows the Block (City-Born origin: Kansas City, Eighteenth Street above all; advantage on Streetwise checks to find a person, place or service in the city)

Favors Owed (Fixer: a pool of 4 favors, refilled each new case or week of downtime; one favor for a name, a dropped charge, a car, a room, a meeting, a file, a warning; two for something big. Every favor spent is owed back; her favors come from Eighteenth Street's own systems, not the machine's, unless she says so)
Know Everybody (Fixer: proficiency bonus doubled for Persuasion and Streetwise checks)

Read the Room (Fixer, 2nd level: after a minute of conversation, Insight against a person's Deception; on a success she learns a goal, a fear or whether one thing said was a lie, and who in the room they fear most)

Circle: City Hall (Fixer, 3rd level: once per case, a city-level favor costs one less, minimum one; she knows which of Horace Quarterman's men can get a thing done downtown, and what they will want for it)
Ability Score Improvement (Fixer, 4th level: +1 Wisdom, +1 Charisma)

Back Door of Every Club (Nightclub Singer background: she can walk in the stage door of any club in town; bartenders, cigarette girls and musicians tell her who was there and who paid; owners give her a booth and an hour)

personality.traits: I am very calm when I am frightened and very funny when I am angry. I write down what everybody owes everybody. I sing under my breath when I think, always the same three bars.
personality.ideals: This street takes care of its own, because nobody else is going to. That means me too.
personality.bonds: The band, ten men and their families who eat because the Jules Ransom Orchestra works. And Jules, who heard me sing at a rent party when I was nineteen and gave me a job the same night.
personality.flaws: There is a record date in Chicago on 12 November, the first of my life, and if Jules is not found the band goes and the date goes with it. Some part of me is counting the days for the wrong reason, and I hate that part, and it does not stop counting.

appearance: A slim, straight-backed Black woman of twenty-seven with a heart-shaped face, wide dark eyes, a small scar at the corner of her mouth, and her hair pressed and pinned under a church hat. By day a plain coat too thin for October; by night a green gown and a voice that fills the Gold Leaf without a microphone.
backstory: Geneva Hollins was born on Vine Street in 1909, the daughter of a laundress and a Pullman porter who was away more than he was home, and sang in the choir at Mount Gilead Baptist before she was old enough to read the hymnal. At nineteen she sang 'Careless Love' at a rent party on the Paseo, and the skinny piano player from Oklahoma who was accompanying her stopped playing in the middle of the second chorus to listen, and hired her before the party was over. She has sung with the Jules Ransom Orchestra for eight years, in every club on Eighteenth Street and on territory tours from Omaha to Oklahoma City in a bus that broke down twice a week. She knows everybody, keeps the band's books, settles the fights, collects from club owners who forget to pay, and has a card file of every favour owed on Eighteenth Street in her own small hand. She is not in love with Jules, whatever anyone says; she is something more durable than that. On Monday morning she took the band's kitty up the stairs over Dandridge's Barber Shop, because the police said a colored musician who stays out late is not a missing person.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Geneva is the client and the campaign's steadiest companion: organised, brave, funny when she is angry, and never helpless. She knows everybody on Eighteenth Street and what they owe each other, and she will use that for the party if they earn it. She is not a love interest and not decoration; she has her own career, her own plans and her own guilt (the Chicago date). Let her run the case board when the table is stuck: her line is 'So what do we actually know?'
dmNotes.voice: Low, warm, precise, a singer's diction; never wastes a word. Calls everybody by their full name until she trusts them, and then by a nickname she invents. When she is frightened, her voice gets quieter and slower, and the party should learn that this is the warning sign.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: find Jules alive. Secondary: keep the band together and working through the winter. Tertiary, and she is ashamed of it: get to Chicago on 12 November.
dmNotes.secrets: She saw Jules hand Lucky a rolled shirt at 4:05 on Sunday morning (clue D1) and has not thought about it once. Second: Horace Quarterman is her godfather, and she has suspected since Sunday that he knows where Jules is, and she has not said so because she cannot bear to be right. Third: she keeps a .32 in her bag and a razor in her garter and has used neither, and has been on a bus at night in Arkansas where she nearly did.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: businesslike, then warm, then fiercely loyal to whoever treats the band as people. Toward Matthias Hartsell: old trust, a little teasing. Toward Beatrice Albright: cool, watchful, then a guarded respect if Beatrice earns it. Toward Lucky Bowden: a sister's protectiveness. Toward Quarterman: love and dread. Toward Virgil Strode, in bn-scenario-004: 'Don't thank me.'
